key_provisions_or_claims: Calls on the Commission to assess including education AI in the high-risk regulatory framework.
Recommends banning automated biometric identification such as facial recognition on educational and cultural premises unless allowed by law.
Requires human supervision of AI decisions affecting educational opportunities; teachers must not be replaced.
Calls for obligatory labelling of deepfakes and AI-generated journalistic text.
Calls for a horizontal AI legal framework, regular independent audits, and clarity on IPR for AI-generated content.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution of 19 May 2021 on AI in education, culture and the audiovisual sector. It urges human-centred, rights-based AI, calls for classifying education AI as potentially high-risk, bans on facial recognition in schools, deepfake labelling, audits, IPR clarification, and digital skills investment. Robotics is mentioned only in passing.
